events.summary: I'd Love to Have You For Dinner Psychological Thriller 2 Acts w/ Intermission 1 Hour 40 Minutes IMPORTANT NOTE: This show contains extreme violence and gore. Viewer discretion is advised. Two lovebirds, Ania and Charles, meet for their first-and-three-quarters date: a home cooked meal. But there is a secret at the table: one of them eats people. The other, of course, is fully aware, because the one who eats people – Ania – is an ancient vampire, while the other – Charles – hunts and eats vampires alive. When these forces – life, and unlife – go for each other’s throats, who will go home with a full stomach? This two act, four-course horror/thriller highlights legacy, cannibalism, the inevitability of personal failure, and the complex moral nature of predation in all its incarnations. Starring: Celah Convis as Ania Komorowski Alex Aho as Charles Marlene Goss as Lady Michele Harte, Director and Writer Julia Lebrell, Stage Manager Max Wray, Marketing

events.title: Off Book: Tour de Force
events.summary: Jessica McKenna and Zach Reino create a completely improvised musical in an attempt to combat the notion that musicals should be “carefully crafted” or “thought out at all.” Jessic and Zach wrote and composed music for the WGA award-winning Peacock Series Baking It starring Maya Rudolph, Amy Poehler and Andy Samberg. Their improvised musical podcast Off Book has been praised by various online publications including Indie Wire, USA Today, Parade, AV Club and Splitsider and been featured at Comedy Central’s Clusterfest Festival, Moontower, the world renowned Just For Laughs Festival in Montreal, and the Netflix Is A Joke Festival in LA. Zach and Jess were listed as one of Vulture’s “Comedians You Should and Will Know” and in early 2019 they released their first full-length musical comedy album The Calendar Album with Comedy Dynamics.

Comedy/Horror One Act - No intermission Running time Approx 70 minutes Join us at the Ant Hall this October for the debut of Planet Ant's original horror comedy, My Daddy is Haunted! events.title: From Frightful to Delightful: East Asian Monsters in the Stacks
events.summary: Celebrate Halloween in the Asia Library, and meet the monsters lurking in our collections! This exhibit brings together demons, shape-shifters, and mythical beasts from across East Asia. You'll discover how those East Asian monstrous creatures have frightened, amused, and fascinated audiences across cultures and generations. Come encounter whimsical and eerie beings that defy easy categorization, and discover what they can tell us about the societies that created and reimagined them. This event offers a playful exploration of East Asian folklore, literature, art, and popular culture. Costumes and curiosity are welcome! Third Thursdays at the Library is a themed monthly open house where we share materials from our collections. While you’re here, pick up a passport and collect a stamp from each of this month's Third Thursday locations — Asia Library, Clark Library, International Studies, and the Special Collections Research Center — to win a prize!

events.title: AIM Seminar:  From woven baskets to filamentous mycelium: harnessing entanglement for structural resilience
events.summary: Abstract: Entanglement of slender elements by interlacing or growing in place offers unique routes to manufacturing composite structural systems with properties that exceed the constituent materials. In this talk, we explore this theme across two systems: woven baskets and mycelium-bound composites. First, we show how weaving thin ribbons into three-dimensional basket shapes creates structures and metamaterials with high stiffness and a remarkable resilience to damage. Experiments and simulations show that woven corners can be as stiff as continuous counterparts made with the same amount of material, yet under large deformations they remain elastic and can fully recover their initial shape, because the interlaced ribbons permit segmented local buckling that deconcentrates stresses. We then show that introducing traditionally unwanted 'snags' into woven systems can engineer the spatial curvature of the thin-sheet system, and that modular assemblies of woven corners can be used to fabricate functional robots that locomote while carrying loads much larger than their self-weight. Second, we turn to mycelium-bound composites, a low-cost, renewable, and biodegradable material made by growing filamentous fungi on lignocellulosic waste. Here, the entanglement is grown rather than woven, and we use pull-out experimental tests to explore the bonding behavior of mycelium. Our results show that mycelium bonds well with all tested materials, including woods, ceramics, metals, polymers, and textiles. Surprisingly, the bonding with Copper, Zinc, Nickel, Iron, and their alloys is particularly strong, as ions from these metals encourage enhanced growth of the mycelium network. Contact: Ian Tobasco

events.title: Everything I Want to Do In a Show | A One Woman Show
events.summary: Hi, I'm Heather Sejnow. You may remember me from such things as that Christmas Commercial for a toy store that gets played every year near St. Claire Shores; hosting shows at the Senate or Redford Theatre as dead celebrities or film characters; or living in Chicago for a short while to do Second City, iO, and then hop back to Detroit to perform at Go Comedy and Planet Ant. I've even nabbed the title of the only female stand up impressionist in the state of Michigan ( that I know of) . I haven't been on a real theatrical performance stage in a while and I'm about to turn 40. So for my mid-life crisis I'm putting on a show of "Everything I Want to Do in a Show". It's campy, crazy, and heartfelt. Most importantly, it's a love letter to everyone I've met and all the vessels of creativity I've learned along the way. Oh! And it's interactive, NSFW, and there will be some prizes for attendees. So come join me on a wild ride filled with puppets, impressions, burlesque, song, dance, and even Shakespeare. It's definitely... "Everything".

events.title: Grand Vision
events.summary: Visiting artist Olayami Dabls is a storyteller, curator, educator, and mentor. He is the founder of the MBAD African Bead Museum in Detroit. Through material culture, Dabls presents commentary on the past, present, and future from African and African-American perspectives, with the understanding that generations of African ancestors used visual materials to convey information about their identity as well as send messages for healing and protection. Dabls is a luminary; for decades he has re-imagined what a museum space can be, accessible to everyone, free from the underpinnings of colonialism and the Western, often white, frame. *Grand Vision* includes a conceptual installation in the Gallery, presenting Dabls’s own work in visual conversation with African beads and artifacts from Dabls’s Bead Museum collections. Additionally, Dabls’s iconic outdoor sculpture *Iron Teaching Rocks Table Manners* will be installed on the U-M campus grounds near UMMA, at the intersection of State Street and South University from September 17- October 11, 2026. The project’s range intends to more fully articulate the many facets of Dabls’ creative practice, and the overlay of art, history, identity, community, and healing.
